vectors.name: formats-xml/basic/interleaved-elements-preserve-order
vectors.comment: A map-of-arrays model cannot represent this interleaving; the edge list can. This is the whole reason the Document is an ordered edge list rather than a map -- confirmed against JSON's own parse of the equivalent {"m":[...]} shape, which cannot preserve this order at all.

vectors.name: formats-xml/basic/attributes-are-dropped-on-read
vectors.comment: The attribute x="1" is gone; there is no path from a Document edge back to an attribute, so writing never produces one either. Confirmed live. D-3 in the divergence ledger notes this is currently dropped silently with no adjustment reported -- omnist-spec#23's error-taxonomy pass should check whether that stays true once format.attribute-dropped is actually emitted.

vectors.name: formats-xml/basic/multi-rooted-document-cannot-be-written
vectors.comment: An XML document has exactly one top-level element; a Document with several top-level edges (legal in JSON/YAML/TOML) has no XML spelling at all. This is exactly why the worked examples in every format page wrap the Order under a single top-level `order` key -- XML alone requires it.
